1	import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';
2	
3	/**
4	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app` ships no TypeScript types (AGENTS.md's "Commerce SDK types not
5	 * importable" gotcha) — `use-toast.js` falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s catch-all
6	 * `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*'` (a shorthand ambient module declaration that
7	 * types the whole module `any` — see that file's own comment, and
8	 * `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s identical narrow-local-type pattern for
9	 * another untyped base function), so the real `useToast()` return value is implicitly `any`.
10	 * Declared narrow here, covering only the two fields this file actually sends (`title`, `status`)
11	 * rather than the base hook's full options surface (`description`, `action`, `position`,
12	 * `duration`, `variant`, `isClosable`) — nothing in this file uses those, so typing them would be
13	 * speculative. `status`'s four values are copied verbatim from the base hook's real accepted set
14	 * (not narrowed to only `'success' | 'warning'`), so a later message that genuinely needs `'error'`
15	 * or `'info'` — SFCC-404's rework, or any message added after this step — is already covered
16	 * without a signature change here.
17	 *
18	 * This is a type annotation documenting an assumed shape, not a runtime guarantee — TypeScript
19	 * allows asserting `any` to any narrower type with no check. The real proof is this file's own
20	 * test, which asserts the exact object the mocked toast function is called with.
21	 */
22	type CartToastStatus = 'success' | 'error' | 'info' | 'warning';
23	type CartToastFn = (options: { title: string; status: CartToastStatus }) => void;
24	
25	/**
26	 * The three real cart messages this step ships, copy verbatim from Figma (SFCC-11 plan step 4.3)
27	 * — this file never derives or paraphrases copy, only interpolates a product name into the one
28	 * message that needs it. SFCC-272's own AC text describes a generic stacked wording ("Item added
29	 * to Wishlist") for when more than one item has been added — deliberately not built here: a toast
30	 * has no aggregation concept, so that copy is only reachable once SFCC-404 ships real message
31	 * stacking. Until then every add uses this product-named variant, one toast per add.
32	 */
33	const getAddedToWishlistMessage = (productName: string): string => `${productName} added to Wishlist`;
34	const ALREADY_IN_WISHLIST_MESSAGE = 'An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist';
35	const MAX_QUANTITY_REACHED_MESSAGE = 'An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity';
36	
37	export type UseCartMessagesReturn = {
38	  /**
39	   * SFCC-272 AC5 — a single product was moved from the cart to the wishlist. `productName` is
40	   * interpolated into the copy on every call — never hardcode a specific product's name at a call
41	   * site. `success` status.
42	   */
43	  notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) => void;
44	  /**
45	   * SFCC-272 AC6 — the item already exists in the shopper's wishlist; the caller leaves the cart
46	   * line untouched. Verbatim copy, no interpolation. `warning` status — see
47	   * `notifyMaxQuantityReached`'s own doc for why cart feedback that doesn't block anything reads
48	   * as a warning in this build, not an error.
49	   */
50	  notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => void;
51	  /**
52	   * CAI-017 / SFCC-250 — a cart line has reached its maximum orderable quantity (the line is
53	   * already capped by `useCartMergeAndCap` before this ever fires). `warning`, not `error`:
54	   * CAI-017's own requirement text says "an error message will be displayed", but the Figma
55	   * rendering uses the warning variant and SFCC-250 AC4 confirms this never blocks checkout — this
56	   * build's own gate resolved the wording as meaning user-facing feedback, not literally Chakra's
57	   * error severity (the same reconciliation `ZimmInlineMessage`'s own `variant` prop documents —
58	   * `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx`: "a caller may
59	   * legitimately pass `variant=\"warning\"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word
60	   * `error`").
61	   */
62	  notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => void;
63	};
64	
65	/**
66	 * Hook — the one surface every cart toast message (success and warning today; whatever SFCC-404's
67	 * real stacking/aggregation rework needs later, including a genuine error) is sent through.
68	 * `emitCartMessage` below is the single call to the underlying toast function — a future rework
69	 * swaps what happens inside this one file, not a hunt across the cart UI for every place that
70	 * fires a toast.
71	 *
72	 * Wraps the **base** `useToast` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast`) rather than a
73	 * new `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` — that path does not exist, and creating it would be an
74	 * unbudgeted Tier 2 change (`protectedFiles.md` would route it to both squads plus tier-2/tier-1
75	 * approvers). See the SFCC-11 plan's own resolved open question 4. This hook is the real "one
76	 * handler" the plan asks for; the base hook underneath it is just the interim renderer SFCC-404
77	 * replaces.
78	 *
79	 * @returns the three named cart-message senders callers actually invoke today. `emitCartMessage`
80	 * itself is intentionally not returned — nothing outside this file needs to send an
81	 * uncatalogued/arbitrary message yet, and a future message is one new named function here, not a
82	 * reason to widen this hook's public surface.
83	 */
84	export const useCartMessages = (): UseCartMessagesReturn => {
85	  // Real return type is implicit `any` (see CartToastFn's own docblock above) — asserted to the
86	  // local narrow type rather than left as `any`, so every call below is checked against the shape
87	  // this file actually depends on.
88	  const toast = useToast() as CartToastFn;
89	
90	  const emitCartMessage = (title: string, status: CartToastStatus): void => {
91	    // SFCC-404: this is the one real call to the underlying toast function. When SFCC-404's real
92	    // stacking/aggregation rework lands, this is the only line that changes.
93	    toast({ title, status });
94	  };
95	
96	  return {
97	    notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) => emitCartMessage(getAddedToWishlistMessage(productName), 'success'),
98	    notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => emitCartMessage(ALREADY_IN_WISHLIST_MESSAGE, 'warning'),
99	    notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => emitCartMessage(MAX_QUANTITY_REACHED_MESSAGE, 'warning'),
100	  };
101	};

/*

 * SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
 * For full license text, see the LICENSE file in the repo root or https://opensource.org/licenses/BSD-3-Clause
 */
import React from 'react'
import {
    Alert,
    AlertIcon,
    AlertTitle,
    CloseButton,
    Spacer,
    useToast as useChakraToast
} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'

/**
 * Display a toast message on the screen.
 * This is a custom hook to handle showing toasts in the app, preventing duplicate toasts and to add action elements
 * to toasts when required. It supports all props supported by Chakra toast.
 *
 * @param {string} title Message text to be displayed in toast
 * @param {string} id - id provided to the toast to avoid duplicate toast ids, use it if multiple toasts are needed
 * @param {string} status Semantic state of the toast - success | error | info | warning
 * @param {node} action Optional component to be displayed in the toast (eg. Button to allow user to perform action)
 * @param {string} position The placement of the toast on screen
 * @param {number} duration The delay before the toast hides (in milliseconds)
 */
export function useToast() {
    const toast = useChakraToast()

    return ({
        title,
        description,
        status,
        action,
        position = 'top-right',
        duration = 5000,
        variant = 'subtle',
        isClosable = true
    }) => {
        let toastConfig = {
            title,
            description,
            status,
            isClosable,
            position,
            duration,
            variant
        }

        if (action) {
            toastConfig = {
                ...toastConfig,

                render: ({onClose}) => (
                    <Alert status={status} variant="subtle" borderRadius="md" py={3} width="sm">
                        <AlertIcon />
                        <AlertTitle> {title} </AlertTitle>
                        <Spacer />
                        {action}
                        <Spacer />
                        <CloseButton onClick={onClose} />
                    </Alert>
                )
            }
        }
        toast(toastConfig)
    }
}

#### Step 4.2 — `useCartMergeAndCap`

**Changes.** One shared function called by both the post-auth callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies.

Settled shape, all of it: threshold **`>=`** not `==` (a line already holding 4 must fail the check, or the `+` stays live exactly when it matters); scope is **per line item**, not per SKU (the SKU is already size + colour, so in normal shopping one line is one SKU); cap **consolidates to one line at 3** (free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single merged line item); callback order **merge → cap → 272's wishlist resume** (the wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing it moves a quantity the shopper never saw); render guard is a secondary backstop that **no-ops while `useIsMutating()` is non-zero**, so it cannot race the callback; **keep the loop guard** — one correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error, because a write-on-render without it can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket; **no action on the brief 4-then-3 flash** — observe real behaviour first.

**Pass criteria.**
1. Unit tests: line at 2 with max 3 → no change. Line at 3 → no change (`>=` boundary, the case `==` gets wrong is 4). Line at 4 → reduced to 3. Line at 5 → reduced to 3. Two lines of the same SKU at 2 each after a `sum_quantities` merge → one consolidated line at 3.
2. `useIsMutating()` non-zero → function returns without issuing a write. Asserted, not assumed.
3. Loop guard: two consecutive invocations against the **same** basket version issue exactly **one** write. A server rejection surfaces an error and does **not** retry indefinitely.
4. Callback order asserted: with all three armed, merge resolves before cap, and cap resolves before the wishlist resume. Assert on call order, not on final state — final state can look right with the wrong order.
5. Max value comes from `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4), not a literal.
6. **State in the PR body that this is not end-to-end verifiable** until SFCC-268's `afterGET` hook is deployed (gate findings #1/#2 — the TSD is `v0.1 Draft`, Technical Lead sign-off Pending, and the live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product, while Jira has 268 as Ready for SIT). The fallback path is what is being tested.

7 of 10 standing angles run; 3 dropped as genuinely vacuous for a 2-file, headless-hook, nothing-renders-it-yet step: **Styling conformance**, **Accessibility**, and **Story interactivity/Real-rendered-layout** (no JSX, no CSS, no story exists — confirmed, not assumed). **React logic correctness** also dropped after inspection: no `useState`/`useEffect`, a single unconditional `useToast()` call — nothing stateful to exercise. Fanned out one sub-agent (independent conformance re-check on the plan-vs-build gap, DRY judgment, and the bypass path) after I'd already done the hands-on work myself (gates, mutation test, base-hook shape); both converged with no disagreement, so no reconciliation was needed.

## Findings by angle

**1. Compiles and passes — CONFIRMED, real numbers, all clean on the step's own files.**
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean, exit 0, zero output.
- `npm run test -- --run`: **119 test files / 1652 tests, all passing** (real run, pasted from output — not the report's claim). Matches the claimed 118→119 / 1646→1652 delta arithmetically (+1 file, +6 tests, all 6 accounted for in `useCartMessages.test.tsx`).
- `npx eslint overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.test.tsx`: clean, exit 0. `npx prettier --check` on both: "All matched files use Prettier code style!"
- **Caveat, not this step's fault:** the real `npm run lint` script (`pwa-kit-dev lint "overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}"`) lints the *whole* overrides tree, not just touched files, and reports **1182 problems (1095 errors, 87 warnings)** project-wide. I grepped that full output for `useCartMessages` — zero hits. This is 100% pre-existing debt in unrelated files (`product-list/index.tsx`, `utils/url.ts`, etc.), not attributable to this step. Reporting the real number because the brief asked for exact output, not a summary — flagged separately below under "what Marcel is missing," not against this step.
- **Mutation test — independently redone by me, not trusted from the report.** I backed up the file (md5 `067116b3a6ea4078f8c328d813ba0a06`), applied two mutations (reordered the interpolation in `getAddedToWishlistMessage`; flipped `notifyMaxQuantityReached`'s status `'warning'`→`'error'`), ran the real suite, then restored byte-for-byte (md5 matched) and re-ran clean. Result: **exactly 4 of 6 tests failed** (`notifyAddedToWishlist` ×2, `notifyMaxQuantityReached` ×2) **and exactly 2 stayed green** (`notifyAlreadyInWishlist`, the shared-emit-path count check) — then all 6 passed again after revert. This exactly matches the Implementer's claimed result. CONFIRMED, independently reproduced.

**2. Tokens — checked, correctly out of scope, not a skip.** `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`'s own header states its scan root as `overrides/app/components/**` and `overrides/app/theme/components/**` only. I ran it for real and grepped the output for `useCartMessages` — zero hits (the 9 unacknowledged violations it did find are all pre-existing, in unrelated `zimmRecentlyViewed*`/`footerShared.ts` files). No `var(--zimm-color-*)` usage exists in either touched file to semantic-check. Clean and genuinely N/A, verified rather than assumed.

**4. Structure — CONFIRMED clean.** `useCartMessages.ts` exports `useCartMessages` matching the filename (components.md > Hooks). JSDoc on the hook includes an explicit `@returns` (line 79). The one `as CartToastFn` assertion (line 88) is backed by a 19-line docblock explaining the untyped-base-module reason (typescript.md's `as`-needs-comment rule). Sub-agent independently grepped both files for `any`, ` as `, `!`, `@ts-ignore` and found the same: every occurrence justified, exactly one `as`, zero bare non-null assertions.

**5. Imports — CONFIRMED clean.** `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` does not exist on disk (`ls` confirms) and has no CODEOWNERS entry for that non-existent path — but I checked CODEOWNERS directly and confirmed line 127 **does** pre-declare `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` as Tier 2 (`@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`), which is exactly why the plan's open-question-4 reasoning for importing the base path instead is real and correct, not just asserted. `useCartMessages.ts` itself has no CODEOWNERS line at all — "untiered," matching the manifest. Single import, no circular risk, no `../../../..` chains. I also read the real base `use-toast.js` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast.js`) directly: it returns a function accepting `{title, description, status, action, position, duration, variant, isClosable}`, calling Chakra's real `toast(toastConfig)` — the test's mock (`useToast: () => mockToast`) is a faithful shape match, not a mock that would silently diverge. This isn't a code defect — the Implementer built exactly what the file manifest said — it's a plan defect needing the same kind of correction note step 4.6 already got, or a decision to build a minimal demo. Flagging for the Scorer since the step's own written pass criteria, read literally, aren't fully satisfied.

**8. Intra-step DRY — checked, judged clean, not a violation.** The three copy strings are defined once as unexported consts in the source and re-typed as literals in the test's assertions. This looks like Angle 8's "typed twice with no shared source" shape, but I concluded it's the correct pattern here, not a defect: for a content/copy-verification test, the test must hold the *Figma-correct* value independently of the implementation — if the test instead imported the source's own constant, the already-run mutation test would prove nothing (a drifted implementation constant would still trivially match itself). Tried to find the pass-criteria-vs-manifest contradiction by treating the plan's own text as adversarial evidence rather than accepting the brief's "nothing else touched" framing at face value — found a real, unacknowledged gap. Tried to find lint/token findings actually attributable to this step by running the full project-wide sweeps and grepping specifically for this step's filename in the output — found none; both are pre-existing debt elsewhere.

I could not verify the Implementer's historical claim of "14 prettier bracket-spacing errors, caught and fixed" as a *before* state — that fix predates my pass and there's nothing left to reproduce; I only confirmed the *current* state is clean (eslint + prettier both exit clean), which is what actually matters for this gate. `npm run lint` run for real against the whole `overrides/` tree currently reports **1095 errors / 87 warnings** project-wide (confirmed live, zero of them in this step's files) — that's a large standing number that isn't this step's doing, but it's worth knowing it's that high before anyone assumes the repo's overall lint state is close to clean.
